panels.figure_caption: Ochronotic pigmentation of calcified articular cartilage. A cross section through the articular surface of the left radial head (post‐fixation) is shown in (a), with the white arrow heads indicating pigmentation of the deep calcified articular cartilage adjacent to the subchondral bone that appears unpigmented. H&E staining of the radial head in is shown in (b) and Schmorl's staining in (c). Pigmented chondrons, indicated by arrows, in (b) and (c) are observed in the calcified articular cartilage (CAC), deep to the tidemark indicated by white arrow heads, and not in the hyaline articular cartilage (HAC). Schmorl's staining of the articular cartilage is shown in (c). Asterisks indicate the position of the cement line separating the CAC from the underlying subchondral bone. The inset in (c), along with (d) and (e), show higher magnification images of pigmented chondrons within the CAC. The arrows in the inset of (c) show a pigmented line connecting adjacent pigmented chondrons and the superficial tidemark.
in_text_mentions: When bisected and photographed, macroscopic pigmentation could be observed deep within the radial head articular cartilage, immediately adjacent to the unpigmented subchondral bone (Figure 9a). From left to right, (e) superior, anterior and inferior views of the talus with arrows indicating areas of pigmentation. The femoral head of the hip joint is shown in (h), with black arrows highlighting pigmentation of the main articular surface, and the white arrows indicating pigmentation of perichondrium. All gross images were taken pre‐fixation, except the bisected radial head images taken post‐fixation in (b).

in_text_mentions: Patient 2 is a 12-year-old female who was noted to have dark urine since early childhood. panels.rationale: This is a substantial single-patient sagittal cervical CT. It directly demonstrates multilevel C4–7 disc-space narrowing and endplate osteophytes, with an arrow indicating ventral degenerative bony change. The caption and disease-focused article title attribute these findings to clinically probable alkaptonuria-associated ochronosis; endplate osteophytes and canal compromise are proposed because they are clearly captioned but absent from the allowed vocabulary. [raw subtype: Ochronotic spondyloarthropathy]

C: Panel C is fat-suppressed T2 sagittal lumbar MRI from same patient, part of Figures 4A-C described as multilevel degenerative changes with disc space narrowing in ochronotic arthropathy case.

(A–C) MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrating multilevel degenerative changes, including mild-to-moderate intervertebral disc space narrowing and reduced T2-weighted signal intensity of the discs, with thickening of the posterior longitudinal ligament. Mild anterior wedge deformities are observed at T11–L1, along with an L3 vertebral compression fracture. Fat-suppressed sequences show patchy hyperintensity within the L1-L3 vertebral bodies, consistent with bone marrow edema.

Sacroiliac MRI confirmed bilateral degenerative changes. SPECT-CT showed increased uptake in shoulders, thoracolumbar and sacral vertebrae, knees, and feet, consistent with chronic inflammatory involvement. Knee ultrasound revealed osteophyte formation, mild synovial proliferation, low-grade synovitis, and minimal effusion. Chest CT and echocardiography were unremarkable.
